key_insight: Randomly sampled triadic interactions in a low-density Fourier-space model still reproduce the core 2D turbulence phenomenology: inverse and direct cascades plus Richardson superdiffusion.
engineering_relevance: This suggests reduced, anisotropic spectral models can capture essential mixing and transport behavior at lower computational cost for turbulence analysis and surrogate modeling.
method: Galerk in-truncated 2D Euler system with retained active/resonant triads
Compare ordered pseudo-logarithmic vs disordered Fourier-space sampling
Vary angular sampling to control anisotropy and triadic density
evidence_signal: Across all configurations, the model shows a $k^{-5/3}$ inverse cascade, a $k^{-3}$ direct cascade, and pair dispersion scaling as $\ell^2(t)\sim t^3$ before crossing to Brownian $\ell^2(t)\sim t$ at long times.
watch_item: Strong spectral anisotropy can alter vorticity organization and flux efficiency, so the method may preserve scaling laws while still biasing amplitudes and short-time transport.
paper_title: Exploring 2D turbulent properties in anisotropic and disordered Fourier space: Insights into inverse cascades and universal superdiffusion from randomly sampled triadic interaction
